POLICE DOCKETS FOR SALE

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An exclusive investigation we catch a cop selling dockets – red handed, on-camera, shamelessly.

Unique Selling Point:
** A CARTE BLANCHE INVESTIGATION
** NO ONE SHOWN THIS ON-CAMERA
** A CONFRONT

Summary:
We’ve all heard it, we’ve done the stories. Way back in 2004 we did a story showing how easy it was to steal a docket. Almost two decades later, dockets still go missing but for a fee. But it’s been near impossible to catch the culprits in the act. Until now. A Carte Blanche viewer steps up to out a corrupt cop peddling criminal police case dockets for cash.

We go undercover and get irrefutable proof.


Further information:
A Carte Blanche viewer’s husband was involved in a car accident that killed a pedestrian child. He was charged with culpable homicide. And the case has been dragging on since 2018. In November 2021, Akasha Ramraj get a whatsapp message from a cop who has plan to make it all go away.

This man, by the name of Kevin, claims the investigation officer passed away and he has taken over the case. For R3500 with the help of the senior public prosecutor the case will be withdrawn and he will give the accused the docket to destroy.

SOUND GOOD, RIGHT? WAIT! IT GETS BETTER!
It’s all on Whatsapp. Detailing everything. And Kevin really is a cop at Lenasia South SAPS – he uses a phone number registered to him. I kid you not! I’ve traced it and linked to him.

He’s been messaging Akasha since November last year. She’s been stringing him along and now decided to contact us. Cop Kevin has dropped the price to R3000.

UNDERCOVER
We go in and buy the docket. He will meet us outside of SAPS and bring the docket to us. All on-camera.

IS THIS AN ISOLATED CASE?
NOPE! Cop Kevin even gives references. He gave two names of people he had helped – I’ve already traced them. And we could make contact with them pretending to want check if he’s for real.

BUST / AUTHORITIES
I need to figure out who we involve – probably SAPS. I’ve already spoken to my cop oracles and figured out how to frame it so that we don’t land in hot water and what exactly to do with the docket once we have it 

INTERVIEWS
1. GARETH NEWHAM – INSTITUTE FOR SECURITY STUDIES // MARK SHAW - GITOC
2. UNDERCOVER ELEMENT
3. AKASHA RAMRAJ – CB VIEWER TO TALK THROUGH THE BACK STORY
4. CONFRONT COP KEVIN GOVENDER
5. SAPS






Extra Budget Items:
EXTRA COSTS
1. THE DOCKET – R3500
2. Investigator fee R2000 – I NEED AN INDIAN MAN TO DO THE UNDERCOVER

** INVESTIGATIVE POTENTIAL – YOU CAN DECIDE AT THE VIEWING

Script:


STRUCTURE
Sequence of crime with dramatic music.

VO: If you do the crime, you should do the time. (prison cell closing)

LINK: But that’s not always the case in South Africa. Criminals often escape prosecution. From technicalities, botched investigations or disappearing dockets.

VO: But dockets don’t just vanish – they are misplaced, they are stolen.

In 2004, we showed just how easy it was for a civilian to walk into a police station, pick up a docket and walk straight out.

Almost two decades later – in many instances dockets are still not kept under lock and key.

LINK: // Beyond incompetence, corruption festers within the criminal justice system – and for a couple of thousand rand, your freedom can be bought.

VO: Yes, police dockets are sold to criminals. And it’s more common than you’d like to believe.

WARREN: if you get caught, this is the only other option to not face jail time.

VO: Warren Lamont is a private investigator with an extensive informant network in the criminal underworld.

WARREN: there are serious cases of armed robbery, murders, CITs. They buy their cases back on a daily basis. M3
DEREK: What sort of bribes are offered?
WARREN: // Up to 30 and 60,000 I've heard of, but mostly on day to day crimes. It's between three and 5000.

VO: It doesn’t matter what the offence is – a crime is a crime - and buying a police docket is illegal. But without concrete proof – it remains urban legend.

We have tried for years to expose this type of corruption, but it’s near impossible. That is until one brave Carte Blanche viewer lifted the veil of secrecy.

AKASHA: I've watched carte blanche for many, many years, from what I see. They try to bring those accountable to book. /

VO: In 2018, Akasha Ramraj’s ex-husband was behind the wheel, when a 10 year old child was run over and killed. He was an unlicensed driver at the time.

The culpable homicide case went to court in 2021. In November that year, Ramraj received these messages from an unknown number.

The person claimed he was from the Lenasia South Police Station, where the case was registered.

AKASHA: I thought maybe statements were outstanding at this stage he thought he was speaking to my ex-husband// the investigating officer started to almost harass me// It just didn't stop. And all it took was 3500 and the case would go away.

VO: To prove he had the docket - he even sent through a photo.

Not sure if she could trust the police, Ramraj decided to hand the evidence to Carte Blanche.

LINK: This is some seriously incriminating evidence, but the police officer didn't hold back one bit in his sales pitch. It's absolutely stunning. This cop is so brazen, he uses his real name and personal cell phone number.

VO: This is the man in question: Kevin Govender - he is actually not an investigating officer but rather an admin clerk at Gauteng’s Lenasia South Police Station. He handles dockets every single day and is shockingly confident about his illegal side hustle.

This message reads… “ No it won’t look suspicious and no one will question anything.”

ZIYANDA: // those are all indicators, you know, of this police officer not doing this for the first time. M12

VO: Author Ziyanda Stuurman is a policing policy researcher.

DEREK: Interesting that he initiated the conversation?
ZIYANDA: This is not a case of somebody being twisted into doing something. They are willingly going out there to find buyers really for these dockets.

VO: Curious to know if dockets truly are up for sale, we decided to send an undercover agent -posing as the suspect's uncle - to meet Kevin Govender.

LINK: When it came to setting up the sting, we didn't know what to expect. After all, the deal was going to go down in the actual police station. And in all honesty, after years of doing this, we still don't want to believe that this level of corruption is really possible.

VO: They meet inside Govender’s office.

BRIEF UPSOUND…. OF CLOSING THE DOOR.

VO: The Culpable Homicide docket is handed over.

AGENT: I checked for the finger prints?
KEVIN: Oh no, that is gone, that will be taken long before – I can’t do that – tell him not to stress. I’ll sort it out .

VO: And Govender takes the cash.

AGENT: I want to give this balance.
KEVIN: for?
AGENT: R3500
KEVIN: oh, yah there was R3000..

VO: Not at all concerned, Govender even continues chatting outside the charge office.

AGENT: But now this case and all is over?
KEVIN: Tell him don’t stress, don’t stress everything is hundreds… But as long as he reads it, then burn it.
AGENT: What is he gonna keep that thing for.
KEVIN: Even if his wife or daughter see that thing, they’re gonna say hey, something’s not right.
AGENT: hmmm
KEVIN: You understand, and then I’m gonna get in trouble.
AGENT: For sure!

VO : Clearly he knows what he’s doing is criminal.

The undercover agent briefed us after his interaction with Govender.

AGENT: this is like part of his business. You go to the shop, you buy something and you get it and you’re gone.
DEREK: Do you get the feeling that he's done this before?
AGENT: Oh, definitely. He's like a pro.

ZIYANDA: This is just another sort of manifestation of really a broken criminal justice system that's failing victims

VO: When dockets go missing, victims are denied justice, crimes go unpunished, and criminals become emboldened.

ZIYANDA: if,, a docket goes missing or there was crucial evidence or information in that docket that can't be replicated or they can't be found again, that absolutely can detrimentally affect the case.

VO: It was time to confront Kevin Govender….so we headed to the Lenasia South Police Station.

LINK: We're going to try and lure him out with our undercover operators. So he's got another accused who wants to buy the docket. Here we go.

VO: As we arrived we saw him ducking into the station.

DEREK: I'm DEREK WATTS from carte blanche. I want to talk to you about selling police dockets.
KEVIN: No, not me, Chief.
DEREK: It’s not you?
DEREK: We’ll show you, i’ve got here, here on video.

VO: Govender was scrambling. He walked up and down with our camera crew in tow.

DEREK Here’s the video of you selling the docket? We've got video evidence that we've got all your whatsapps.

VO: Realising he was in trouble, he didn’t know where to turn.

KEVIN: Okay Chief, thank you. I’ll get my lawyer to contact you.
DEREK: Okay, so you admit that it's you.
KEVIN: No, it’s not me.

VO: It seemed we had a runner - Govender took off on foot.

DEREK: You were paid three and a half thousand rands. M4
KlEVIN: No I wasn’t
DEREK: If you're not guilty, why are you running away?
KEVIN: I’m not running away.

VO: Well you could have fooled us. Despite the denials - he is the same man caught on camera in the undercover sting.

DEREK: We've got the picture here. You've got the picture. This is you. Yeah.
KEVIN: Somebody can use my picture, boss.

VO: Nope, look at this video clip again. This is not someone using his picture. This is him, Kevin Govender, selling an active police docket.

LINK: That’s all we’re going to see or hear of Kevin Govender today.

VO: Brigadier Richard Shibiri is the Provincial Head for Crime Investigation Services in Gauteng.

DEREK: Brigadier, we're told that those involved in cash in transit heists, armed robbers, murderers, just buy dockets on a weekly basis
BRIG: Yes, we’ll appreciate if such information is brought before us so that we can investigate and verify But where I'm standing, I don't have any reports to say there were dockets sold or missing.
DEREK: I'd like you to look at this. It's a case docket, and we'd like your opinion regarding whether it is legitimate or not, because that was sold to an undercover operator for three and a half thousand rands.
BRIG: Yeah, from the observation, it is a true docket. Case docket.
DEREK: Brigadier, This is a culpable homicide case. A child died. The driver was unlicensed. Does this concern you?
BRIG: Yes. It is very concerning that you came with a docket and you indicate you bought it.

VO: We returned the docket, without compromising it and showed the Brigadier the hidden camera footage.

DEREK: Well, the police employee in question sold a docket inside the Lenasia South Police Station. He clearly had no regard for the law.
BRIG: this is unacceptable. , we will have to investigate and get to the bottom of this and make sure that the culprits are brought to book.

ZIYANDA: This is a serious offense. And I think this really speaks to a breakdown in the disciplinary function of the SAPS. They're operating with a level of impunity. And unfortunately for us, some cops and to see it as a as a revenue stream.

VO: While disappearing dockets raise questions about police case management systems - the Brigadier insists it’s not a challenge.

BRIG: Since the introduction of the e-docket, it's not much of an issue because when the case is lost, we or is missing. We are able to retrieve the docket.
DEREK: So, Brigadier, are you confident in telling us that virtually every case docket is scanned?
BRIG: That is correct.

VO: Despite various enquiries, the police would not confirm when and whether the docket in question was scanned entirely - only stating that “all index pages” were scanned and “an investigation has been launched.”

LINK: While the police are adamant that the e-docket system is working, it's by no means foolproof. There's plenty of room for collusion between cops and court officials.

VO: A prosecutor can decide to withdraw a case if the docket is not in court, and even if there is an e-docket it may not have every single page scanned in, and if it has all the pages, the authenticity of some of the documents could be called into question in court.

ZIYANDA: / the creation of an e-docket system won't completely eliminate the possibility of tampering or malpractice with dockets. Really making cases disappear against people is the absolute antithesis of the type of work that police officers should be doing.

VO: Akasha Ramraj hopes that speaking up will help bring about change.

AKASHA: I want justice to be served. I don't want to live in a country where it's so easy to buy dockets and just make the case disappear.

metadata.Summary: We’ve all heard it, we’ve done the stories. Way back in 2004 we did a story showing how easy it was to steal a docket. Almost two decades later, dockets still go missing but for a fee. But it’s been near impossible to catch the culprits in the act. Until now. A Carte Blanche viewer steps up to out a corrupt cop peddling criminal police case dockets for cash. We go undercover and get irrefutable proof.
metadata.Further information: A Carte Blanche viewer’s husband was involved in a car accident that killed a pedestrian child. He was charged with culpable homicide. And the case has been dragging on since 2018. In November 2021, Akasha Ramraj get a whatsapp message from a cop who has plan to make it all go away. This man, by the name of Kevin, claims the investigation officer passed away and he has taken over the case. For R3500 with the help of the senior public prosecutor the case will be withdrawn and he will give the accused the docket to destroy. SOUND GOOD, RIGHT? WAIT! IT GETS BETTER! It’s all on Whatsapp. Detailing everything. And Kevin really is a cop at Lenasia South SAPS – he uses a phone number registered to him. I kid you not! I’ve traced it and linked to him. He’s been messaging Akasha since November last year. She’s been stringing him along and now decided to contact us. Cop Kevin has dropped the price to R3000. UNDERCOVER We go in and buy the docket. He will meet us outside of SAPS and bring the docket to us. All on-camera. IS THIS AN ISOLATED CASE? NOPE! Cop Kevin even gives references. He gave two names of people he had helped – I’ve already traced them. And we could make contact with them pretending to want check if he’s for real. BUST / AUTHORITIES I need to figure out who we involve – probably SAPS. I’ve already spoken to my cop oracles and figured out how to frame it so that we don’t land in hot water and what exactly to do with the docket once we have it  INTERVIEWS 1. GARETH NEWHAM – INSTITUTE FOR SECURITY STUDIES // MARK SHAW - GITOC 2. UNDERCOVER ELEMENT 3. AKASHA RAMRAJ – CB VIEWER TO TALK THROUGH THE BACK STORY 4. CONFRONT COP KEVIN GOVENDER 5. SAPS
metadata.Extra Budget Items: EXTRA COSTS 1. THE DOCKET – R3500 2. Investigator fee R2000 – I NEED AN INDIAN MAN TO DO THE UNDERCOVER ** INVESTIGATIVE POTENTIAL – YOU CAN DECIDE AT THE VIEWING
